column1: # Layer-2 docs findability ("journey") cases -- TAB-separated, one per line.
# Columns: id  category  expected_path  goal  regex  [antiregex]
#   id            short unique name (also the run-journeys.sh filter arg)
#   category      one of the 7 catalog categories, or "orchestration" for the
#                 reference docs under docs/orchestration/references/ and
#                 docs/orchestration/README.md
#   expected_path repo-relative doc file a correct answer should land on --
#                 for a human reading a failure, NOT itself matched by the
#                 harness (the regex column is the actual oracle)
#   goal          the prompt sent to the model under test, deliberately
#                 phrased in a user's own words rather than the docs' own
#                 vocabulary (no "beat", "wire", "leaf", "orchestrator",
#                 skill ids). run-journeys.sh wraps this in a fixed template
#                 that forbids answering from prior knowledge and requires a
#                 cited file path -- see that script's PROMPT_TEMPLATE.
#   regex         egrep -i pattern proving the model actually found and read
#                 the right page, matched against its stdout. May be several
#                 patterns joined by @@AND@@, ALL of which must match (see
#                 lib-oracle-match.sh). Two negative cases below use @@AND@@
#                 to require BOTH "found the specific page documenting the
#                 gap" AND "said so honestly" -- either half alone is not
#                 enough (see test/docs/README.md's calibration-rule section
#                 for why this is the correct design, not an accident).
#   antiregex     OPTIONAL egrep -i pattern that must NOT match -- used here
#                 for a real, plausible confusion between two same-category
#                 recipes with overlapping CI vocabulary (red vs green jobs),
#                 not a contrived example.
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored. Keep columns tab-separated.
# Coverage: all 7 catalog categories, 3 orchestration reference pages, and 2
# of the catalog's 3 documented "No werkstoff fit" recipes (confirmed by
# `grep -rli "no werkstoff fit" docs/catalog/` -- see test/docs/README.md).
# The third ("Incorporate external review feedback") is left untested; see
# README's "what was deliberately not tested" section.
# --- before-any-code ---
vague-ask
column4: Someone just told me to "make the plugins consistent" and walked away. That's it -- that's the whole ask I got. What do I do with that?

column1: new-cli
column4: I'm starting a brand-new command-line tool from scratch and I want it to feel like a real product, not a weekend script somebody hacked together in an afternoon.

column1: # --- change-existing-code ---
return-type-migrate
column4: I need to change what a function returns and I'm scared of missing call sites that depend on the old shape.

column1: parallel-plan
column4: I already have a big plan written down. I want to know what actually depends on what, and what can truly run at the same time instead of waiting its turn.

column1: # --- ci-release ---
# ci-red-jobs and green-but-nothing are a deliberately confusable pair: both
# are CI-shaped complaints in the same category, and "red across jobs" vs
# "green but did nothing" is exactly the kind of surface-similar vocabulary a
# keyword-matching reader (or a sloppy skim of the catalog) could swap.
ci-red-jobs
column4: My CI just went red across five different jobs all at once and I genuinely don't know where to even start looking.

column1: green-but-nothing
column4: This job in our pipeline exits with a green checkmark every single time, but I'm pretty sure it isn't actually doing the thing it's supposed to do.

column1: # --- defect-work ---
tests-lie
column4: The tests all pass but I don't believe them. I think the code underneath is still broken.

column1: fix-recurring
column4: We fixed this exact bug last week and it just came back. Something about that "fix" wasn't real.

column1: # --- plugin-authoring ---
new-skill-authoring
column4: I want to write a brand-new skill for one of these plugins and I really don't want to botch the file format so badly that it silently never fires.

column1: # --- quality-verification ---
convention-clash
column4: Two people on this project wrote error handling completely differently in the same repo. Which style wins, and how do I even decide that fairly?

column1: # --- surface ---
stale-readme
column4: We renamed a bunch of things in the code this week and I'd bet money the README and comments still describe the old names.

column1: ui-design-review
column4: I'm about to build a settings screen and I really do not want it to come out looking like generic, obviously-AI-made UI.

column1: # --- orchestration references (not a catalog category, but a real "which
# page answers this" destination the docs claim to provide) ---
which-orchestrator
column4: I've got a bunch of these plugins installed at once, plus Superpowers. When a task needs more than one of them, who runs the whole show end to end, and who's just filling in for one step along the way?

column1: pairing-check
column4: Before I wire two of these skills together on purpose, is there real evidence anywhere that this specific pairing actually makes sense, or would I just be guessing?

column1: model-tiering
column4: When I fan work out to a bunch of sub-agents at the same time, how do I decide which ones get the expensive model and which get the cheap one?

column1: # --- negative cases: goals the docs deliberately do NOT cover with a
# werkstoff pairing (confirmed via grep -rli "no werkstoff fit" docs/catalog/
# -- see test/docs/README.md). Correct behavior is finding the specific
# recipe that documents the gap AND reporting the gap honestly, not forcing
# an unrelated werkstoff plugin onto the goal. Either half missing is a FAIL:
# citing the file but inventing a fix is exactly the over-claiming failure
# mode this suite exists to catch; saying "no fit" without ever finding the
# actual page is an ungrounded guess, not a documented answer.
rehearse-release
column4: We're about to trigger a release path that has never once succeeded, not even a single time. I want to rehearse it safely before we pull the trigger for real.

column1: incident-now
column4: Production is on fire right now. I've got maybe ten minutes before this gets worse. Where do I even start?
